properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245), which labels this feature directly (not inferred). Georeferenced using an affine transform fit from 8 control points -- the 4 real-world corners of Block 1 and the 4 real-world corners of Block 12 (both already independently traced and committed elsewhere in this dataset), matched to their pixel positions in this same diagram. Residual error against those 8 control points is roughly 15-24m, consistent with this site's other entries. This is a DIFFERENT (but equivalent-precision) point set than the 9 street-intersection points used for Blocks 1-15 -- both were derived from the same source diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-15: user-flagged visual check found this polygon sitting mostly in the water, not on the real shoreline -- confirmed by pixel-sampling the actual water/land color transition along the coast at several latitudes, which showed the traced strip running consistently ~12m east of the true shoreline (the 8-control-point transforms residual error, landing on the water side rather than the land side). Shifted the entire polygon 12m west (bearing 266.5, this site's established grid west direction) as a uniform correction, preserving the traced shape's relative geometry -- overlay-confirmed afterward that the shifted strip now sits on the real paved/rocky shoreline strip for its full length, including through the point/breakwater curve at the south end. Not a full re-trace of the curve's own shape -- see accuracy_caveat. SECOND CORRECTION 2026-09-15: user confirmed the 12m uniform shift still left most of the shape (especially the southern point/breakwater curve) sitting in the water -- a single uniform shift could not fix a curving coastline traced from a diagram. Re-traced from scratch directly off satellite color: classified water vs. land per-pixel (water reads distinctly greener/cyan relative to red -- G-R > 12 -- versus this industrial sites darker, warmer-toned dirt and pavement) at zoom 19, scanned every ~8th row for the first sustained water run to get a raw shoreline point per row, then smoothed with a median filter (window 15, then 9) to cancel wave-texture noise while preserving the real curve including the point at the south end. Built the park as an 8m-wide ribbon (this sites established grid bearing, 266.5 degrees, for the inland offset) along that traced shoreline. Overlay-confirmed the full length, including the point curve, now sits on real land. RE-CLIPPED 2026-09-16: user spotted this feature still visibly cutting into Block 9 on the rendered map -- the earlier same-day fix only avoided reusing this trace's bad segment when building the new Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area) connector, but never corrected this file's own geometry, so the original notch (dipping into Block 9's now-corrected footprint) was still here. Clipped this polygon directly against Block 9's own current geometry via shapely difference() -- Block 9's boundary cuts all the way through this thin ribbon at that point, so the result is a MultiPolygon (the ribbon north of Block 9 and the ribbon south of it, both real portions, now with zero overlap into Block 9 by construction rather than by hand-editing vertices). 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source_doc_urls entry pointed to the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the Design for Development (potrero_power_D4D_draft-082219.pdf), which now returns 404 and has no archive snapshot; it has been repointed to the adopted final D4D (February 26, 2020, https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) and Table 3.1.1 Permitted Uses on printed p.47, and whose footers carry the February 26, 2020 date; the SF Planning project page (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station) is added as the source for status and phasing. The park's shoreline shape itself was re-traced from satellite imagery as described above, so digitized_from's citation of Figure 6.2.3 covers only the park's name and general location ('WATERFRONT PARK' is labelled vertically along the shoreline east of Block 9 and the Stack in the final figure); the full extent is shown in the final D4D's Figure 4.16.1. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this as a long, curving shoreline strip running the full length of the site's bay frontage (continuing north and south beyond this figure's own page crop in the source PDF). This polygon traces only the portion visible on Figure 6.2.3 itself as a simplified strip (not the full shoreline extent, and not precisely following the actual curving shore/site-boundary line, which was simplified to a handful of vertices). Treat as directionally correct but incomplete and shape-approximate. Same 15-25m positional tolerance as this site's other entries. Position corrected 2026-09-15 (12m uniform shift onto the real shoreline, see digitization_method) -- the strip's own curve/shape still was not independently re-verified vertex-by-vertex against the coastline, only its overall position. Second position correction 2026-09-15: re-traced directly from satellite imagery color (water vs. land pixel classification), not the diagram transform -- now an 8m-wide ribbon on the real shoreline, including the southern point/breakwater curve. Still simplified (does not capture the D4D-labeled strips full north-south extent beyond what is visible here) and the exact width (8m) is an assumption, not measured from any park-design source. NOTE 2026-09-16: this feature's own outer-shoreline trace turned out to substantially overlap the newly-added 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)' -- evidence (a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline listing describing the same corridor as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', which could not be located or checked) suggests both features describe the same physical shoreline strip: this one as the D4D's own long-term planning label, Prequel Park as the interim park (still planned: the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 says the developer hoped to start construction in the third quarter of 2026, and no source confirms a start). The overlap is expected, not a tracing error -- see Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)'s own digitization_method. Not merged into one feature since the two have different sourcing/status and either could be independently corrected later.'; notes: 'Simplified partial trace of a long shoreline open space -- see accuracy_caveat; does not capture the strip's full north-south extent.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The Port shoreline premises are Port land under Lease L-16662 (Port Commission memo, Nov 14, 2025); DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, and whether any of them matches this park was not checked.'.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this as a long, curving shoreline strip running the full length of the site's bay frontage (continuing north and south beyond this figure's own page crop in the source PDF). This polygon traces only the portion visible on Figure 6.2.3 itself as a simplified strip (not the full shoreline extent, and not precisely following the actual curving shore/site-boundary line, which was simplified to a handful of vertices). Treat as directionally correct but incomplete and shape-approximate. Same 15-25m positional tolerance as this site's other entries. Position corrected 2026-09-15 (12m uniform shift onto the real shoreline, see the mapping log in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record)) -- the strip's own curve/shape still was not independently re-verified vertex-by-vertex against the coastline, only its overall position. Second position correction 2026-09-15: re-traced directly from satellite imagery color (water vs. land pixel classification), not the diagram transform -- now an 8m-wide ribbon on the real shoreline, including the southern point/breakwater curve. Still simplified (does not capture the D4D-labeled strips full north-south extent beyond what is visible here) and the exact width (8m) is an assumption, not measured from any park-design source. NOTE 2026-09-16: this feature's own outer-shoreline trace turned out to substantially overlap the newly-added 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)' -- evidence (a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline listing describing the same corridor as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', which could not be located or checked) suggests both features describe the same physical shoreline strip: this one as the D4D's own long-term planning label, Prequel Park as the interim park (still planned: the Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 says the developer hoped to start construction in the third quarter of 2026, and no source confirms a start). The overlap is expected, not a tracing error -- see Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)'s own mapping log. Not merged into one feature since the two have different sourcing/status and either could be independently corrected later.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) The Port shoreline premises are Port land under Lease L-16662 (Port Commission memo, Nov 14, 2025); DataSF Parcels (queried 2026-09-29) lists active lots in Assessor blocks 4175 and 4232 added in December 2023 after the Phase 1 Final Map, and whether any of them matches this park was not checked.
properties.regulatory_context: The site's shoreline public-access open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label, running along the bay side of Blocks 9 and the Stack, connecting toward Warm Water Cove Park to the south (shown on the same figure, outside the project site boundary).
properties.notes: Simplified partial trace of a long shoreline open space -- see the accuracy caveat; does not capture the strip's full north-south extent.
